summary: Most sophisticated OT probe in this tranche. Reaches T2 in three places: WriteProperty dry-run (reads then re-writes the same bytes at priority 16 → SimpleAck is direct proof of unauth write to a physical point), DCC accepted with default password (proves DoS primitive), and ReinitializeDevice accepted with intentionally-bad password (proves remote reboot with no password check). Also does AtomicReadFile (returns actual file bytes — arguably T2 file-read). Gap: no BACnet/SC posture check beyond port co-presence; amplification finding could be measured against a spec-corpus ratio.

findings.title_pattern: BACnet/IP endpoint reachable (unauthenticated building-automation control plane)
findings.tier_evidence: I-Am reply after unicast Who-Is is deterministic BACnet fingerprint.
findings.promotion_notes: Already promoted by bacnet_unauth_write (T2) and bacnet_reinitialize_permitted (T2).
findings.tester_next_step: bacnet-discover -a <ip>; then walk the object list (bacwi -1 <ip>) and read Device object properties (bacrp <ip> device <inst> object-name).

findings.promotion_notes: Add vendor→CVE map (Siemens Desigo, JCI Metasys, Distech, Automated Logic) so vendor_name+firmware pins known BAS advisories.
findings.tester_next_step: Cross-reference vendor/model against ICSA-* BAS advisories; check the corresponding web UI on 80/443/8080 for default creds — Siemens Desigo: admin/admin, JCI Metasys: MetasysSysAgent/MetasysSysAgent.

findings.title_pattern: BACnet object inventory readable without authentication
findings.tier_evidence: Object-list walk returns real object type/instance tuples — enumerates physical points.
findings.promotion_notes: Pair with bacnet_unauth_write to prove per-object writability; expand walk beyond max_entries=32 under --bacnet-full-walk.
findings.tester_next_step: bacwi -1 <ip>; for each analog-value: bacrp <ip> analog-value <inst> present-value; identify high-value points (chillers, dampers, door-strikes) by object-name field.

findings.title_pattern: BACnet BBMD Broadcast-Distribution-Table readable (network topology disclosure)
findings.tier_evidence: Read-BDT (BVLC 0x02) reply contains real peer BBMD IPs/masks — deterministic topology.
findings.promotion_notes: Chain: use each BDT peer as a follow-on scan target; run bacnet.probe against every peer to build cross-site BAS map.
findings.tester_next_step: For each BDT entry, run bacnet-discover -a <peer_ip>; the BDT maps the entire multi-site BAS. On corp-reachable BBMDs this reveals sites behind NAT.

findings.tier_evidence: Read-FDT reply lists foreign-registered peers with TTL — real remote endpoints.
findings.promotion_notes: Each FDT entry is a jump-target (engineering laptop or cloud gateway); probe it for HMI/web UI defaults.
findings.tester_next_step: For each FDT entry, nmap -sV -p 80,443,8080,47808 <peer_ip>; often the peer is an engineer's Windows workstation with SMB/RDP open.

findings.title_pattern: BACnet Foreign-Device registration accepted from arbitrary host
findings.promotion_notes: Once registered, send Distribute-Broadcast (0x09) to inject broadcast frames site-wide; PoC only under --bacnet-write.
findings.tester_next_step: bacnet-fdr-register <ip>:47808 --ttl 60; then broadcast a Who-Is via the BBMD and receive I-Am from every peer segment — proves segment-wide read from an off-site host.

findings.title_pattern: BACnet/IP acts as UDP amplification reflector (Who-Is/I-Am ratio)
findings.tier_evidence: Actual measured request/reply byte ratio ≥3.0 and reply_count ≥2 — deterministic reflection factor.
findings.promotion_notes: Promoting further requires generating spoofed traffic — out of scope for a defensive scanner.
findings.tester_next_step: hping3 -1 --spoof <victim> <ip> -d 12 -c 1 (with a Who-Is payload) — DO NOT run at Internet scale; corroborate the ratio only.

findings.title_pattern: BACnet WriteProperty accepted without authentication (physical-process write)
findings.tier_evidence: WriteProperty of the same bytes just read at priority 16 returned SimpleAck — direct proof unauth writes land on a real Analog-Value object. Not destructive because value is unchanged.
findings.promotion_notes: T3 would be a targeted write at priority 1 to a specific commandable point (door unlock, setpoint change) — physical actuation. Requires operator approval; recce should never do this by default.
findings.tester_next_step: TEST-CELL ONLY: bacwp -1 -p 47808 <ip> 2 <av_inst> 85 1 4 <new_val>; verify with bacrp then restore. Never against production.

findings.title_pattern: BACnet DeviceCommunicationControl accepted with empty/default password (DoS primitive)
findings.tier_evidence: DCC SimpleAck with a known default password (or empty) is proof the DoS primitive works. Recce sends duration=1min not 0 for safety.
findings.promotion_notes: T3 (destructive) would be duration=0 = indefinite comms disable, or DCC with a stronger valid default from vendor docs.
findings.tester_next_step: TEST-CELL ONLY: bacdcc -p 47808 <ip> --disable --duration 0 --password '<accepted_pw>' — brings the controller offline until manual re-enable. Never on production.

findings.title_pattern: BACnet ReinitializeDevice reachable without valid password (remote reboot)
findings.tier_evidence: SimpleAck to WARMSTART with a deliberately BAD password is deterministic proof the device never validates — reboot is one packet away.
findings.promotion_notes: T3 (destructive) = actually send the reboot; recce correctly refuses. Under --bacnet-reboot in a test cell only.
findings.tester_next_step: TEST-CELL ONLY: bacrd -p 47808 <ip> warmstart; observe the controller reboot and all points drop for the boot cycle.

findings.title_pattern: BACnet AtomicReadFile returned file contents without authentication
findings.tier_evidence: AtomicReadFile (0x06) returns actual bytes from a File object — that IS file-content exfiltration, not stance.
findings.promotion_notes: Bump read count from 32 to full file size under --bacnet-file-dump; look for controller backup/config files that contain credentials.
findings.tester_next_step: bacnet-atomic-read -p 47808 <ip> 10 <file_inst> 0 65535; save to disk and strings/hex it — look for admin creds, WPA keys, BMS API keys embedded in config backups.

findings.tier_evidence: max-APDU + segmentation — passive fingerprint, no vuln evidence.
findings.promotion_notes: Cross-reference the (max_apdu, segmentation, vendor_id) tuple against known parser-DoS advisories (BACnet stack CVE list).
findings.tester_next_step: Correlate small max-APDU + segmented-both against BACnet-stack DoS CVEs — e.g. Trane/SmartX / Cimetrics / Delta Controls parser bugs; do NOT fuzz against production.

findings.title_pattern: BACnet Secure Connect (BACnet/SC) present alongside plaintext BACnet/IP (downgrade path)
findings.tier_evidence: Both 47820/tcp and 47808/udp open on same host is deterministic downgrade posture.
findings.promotion_notes: Already the full story — evidence is port co-presence.
findings.tester_next_step: nmap -p 47820,47808 <ip>; confirm both open then talk plaintext to 47808 to prove downgrade works even though /SC exists on 47820.
